Run locally

From a checkout with Nix and Devenv installed, enter the development shell, install the locked dependencies, then start the API and site together.

The Studio runs at localhost:5173/gui/. Its same-origin /api proxy reaches the Baste server on port 3456. Set BASTE_SITE_PORT and BASTE_API_PORT to change the ports. Storybook is an optional process on port 6006.

Use the native tasks for individual commands and checks. The full task list and environment setup live in the development guide.

Configure an account server

In Studio Settings, select Sign in / create profile. Not Organic creates or authenticates your account profile; a Baste design persona is a separate object. Manage your handle and account in the linked Not Organic portal.

The Baste server holds the provider session and DPoP key. The browser receives an HttpOnly Baste session cookie, a CSRF token and the profile's public DID and handle. The model picker loads the authorized catalog from your connected account.

Your wallet shows verified available credit and only the offers advertised by the provider. Select an offer to open checkout and review its current price before paying. On return, refresh the wallet: a redirect alone does not prove payment or credit delivery.

Hosted generation currently covers image suites and asset judging. Full UI kits still need your local SVG and video providers. An unverified, blocked or empty wallet prevents paid hosted generation; prompt drafts remain available.

Set a maximum spend for each hosted run, initially $1. The live budget plan counts image and judging requests, including QD candidates and final outputs. Reduce iterations, batch size or outputs per purpose until the plan fits your maximum and the server limit, or explicitly raise your maximum. These conservative ceilings are spending limits, not quoted prices.

For server operators: enable NOTORGANIC_ENABLED, set BASTE_PUBLIC_ORIGIN, and configure the issuer and authorization URL. Baste must be registered with Not Organic for its origin, callback, product audience, scopes and billing offers. Public checkout needs an HTTPS return origin.

The callback is /api/notorganic/callback on the Studio origin. Production hosting must proxy /api to the Baste server. Sessions live in server memory and expire after eight hours; restarting the server requires signing in again. Read the account integration guide for the deployment boundary.

Use your own provider keys

Local mode keeps provider keys in the server environment or local config. Image generation uses OpenAI or Google; SVG generation uses QuiverAI; video uses its configured provider. The Studio never needs an upstream key pasted into a form.

Copy .env.example to .env and configure only the services you use. Run baste config --init to create baste.config.json. Model IDs must be supported by your chosen provider. Local generation and CLI use this configuration; hosted Studio requests use the connected account session.

Companion voice

Set FAL_KEY on the Baste API server for ElevenLabs Turbo v2.5 speech and Wizper transcription. The browser sends recorded audio to Baste and receives audio bytes or editable text; it never receives the provider key. Recording starts only after a user gesture and stops after 45 seconds.

The Skate option reads fal_api_key@secrets into the API process environment. Alternatively set FAL_KEY in your server environment. The fal account needs available credit. Set BASTE_VOICE_ENABLED=false to disable voice.

Hosted account mode additionally requires BASTE_VOICE_ENABLED=true. Existing account authentication, origin and CSRF checks apply. Voice uses the operator’s fal balance, separately from Not Organic wallet billing. Each server process allows ten requests per caller per minute, 120 total per hour, and four concurrent requests; replicated deployments need a shared limit before increasing capacity.

Speech and transcription use bounded, cancellable requests. Audio is not saved by Baste. fal receives the audio and text, with provider request storage disabled. Spoken replies require an explicit opt-in. Pause, resume, stop, persona changes and tab visibility control playback and microphone cleanup.

This is turn-based voice with editable transcripts. The planned GPT-Live design partner remains a separate integration. Voice does not turn the authored guided demo into a model conversation.

CLI reference

The CLI operates on your local persona store. It does not inherit a Studio account session. Use baste --help for versioning, remix, site decomposition, cultural references and OpenPencil commands.

Local output lives under assets/output/: SVGs, images, videos, plus a persona suite manifest with metadata and relationships. In account mode, persona records and assets belong to the authenticated DID's separate directory.

The quality-diversity archive explores color temperature, visual density and abstractness. Judging weights persona alignment at 30%, visual quality and uniqueness at 20% each, coherence and usability at 15% each. These scores guide selection; review assets in the interface they will serve.

Run your own Baste installation, configure generation services, or build with the CLI and API.

Looking for help with personas, materials, moodboards or exports? Read the Studio guide.

{SECTIONS.map(([id, label]) => {label})}

Run locally

From a checkout with Nix and Devenv installed, enter the development shell, install the locked dependencies, then start the API and site together.

The Studio runs at localhost:5173/gui/. Its same-origin /api proxy reaches the Baste server on port 3456. Set BASTE_SITE_PORT and BASTE_API_PORT to change the ports. Storybook is an optional process on port 6006.

Use the native tasks for individual commands and checks. The full task list and environment setup live in the development guide.

Configure an account server

In Studio Settings, select Sign in / create profile. Not Organic creates or authenticates your account profile; a Baste design persona is a separate object. Manage your handle and account in the linked Not Organic portal.

The Baste server holds the provider session and DPoP key. The browser receives an HttpOnly Baste session cookie, a CSRF token and the profile's public DID and handle. The model picker loads the authorized catalog from your connected account.

Your wallet shows verified available credit and only the offers advertised by the provider. Select an offer to open checkout and review its current price before paying. On return, refresh the wallet: a redirect alone does not prove payment or credit delivery.

Hosted generation currently covers image suites and asset judging. Full UI kits still need your local SVG and video providers. An unverified, blocked or empty wallet prevents paid hosted generation; prompt drafts remain available.

Set a maximum spend for each hosted run, initially $1. The live budget plan counts image and judging requests, including QD candidates and final outputs. Reduce iterations, batch size or outputs per purpose until the plan fits your maximum and the server limit, or explicitly raise your maximum. These conservative ceilings are spending limits, not quoted prices.

For server operators: enable NOTORGANIC_ENABLED, set BASTE_PUBLIC_ORIGIN, and configure the issuer and authorization URL. Baste must be registered with Not Organic for its origin, callback, product audience, scopes and billing offers. Public checkout needs an HTTPS return origin.

The callback is /api/notorganic/callback on the Studio origin. Production hosting must proxy /api to the Baste server. Sessions live in server memory and expire after eight hours; restarting the server requires signing in again. Read the account integration guide for the deployment boundary.

Use your own provider keys

Local mode keeps provider keys in the server environment or local config. Image generation uses OpenAI or Google; SVG generation uses QuiverAI; video uses its configured provider. The Studio never needs an upstream key pasted into a form.

Copy .env.example to .env and configure only the services you use. Run baste config --init to create baste.config.json. Model IDs must be supported by your chosen provider. Local generation and CLI use this configuration; hosted Studio requests use the connected account session.

Companion voice

Set FAL_KEY on the Baste API server for ElevenLabs Turbo v2.5 speech and Wizper transcription. The browser sends recorded audio to Baste and receives audio bytes or editable text; it never receives the provider key. Recording starts only after a user gesture and stops after 45 seconds.

The Skate option reads fal_api_key@secrets into the API process environment. Alternatively set FAL_KEY in your server environment. The fal account needs available credit. Set BASTE_VOICE_ENABLED=false to disable voice.

Hosted account mode additionally requires BASTE_VOICE_ENABLED=true. Existing account authentication, origin and CSRF checks apply. Voice uses the operator’s fal balance, separately from Not Organic wallet billing. Each server process allows ten requests per caller per minute, 120 total per hour, and four concurrent requests; replicated deployments need a shared limit before increasing capacity.

Speech and transcription use bounded, cancellable requests. Audio is not saved by Baste. fal receives the audio and text, with provider request storage disabled. Spoken replies require an explicit opt-in. Pause, resume, stop, persona changes and tab visibility control playback and microphone cleanup.

This is turn-based voice with editable transcripts. The planned GPT-Live design partner remains a separate integration. Voice does not turn the authored guided demo into a model conversation.

CLI reference

The CLI operates on your local persona store. It does not inherit a Studio account session. Use baste --help for versioning, remix, site decomposition, cultural references and OpenPencil commands.

Errors distinguish authentication (401), denied access (403), insufficient credit (402), busy provider (429), and unavailable services. Config writes and native file/watch operations are unavailable in account mode. The README contains the wider local API and TypeScript package usage.

Keep the fitting

Local output lives under assets/output/: SVGs, images, videos, plus a persona suite manifest with metadata and relationships. In account mode, persona records and assets belong to the authenticated DID's separate directory.

The quality-diversity archive explores color temperature, visual density and abstractness. Judging weights persona alignment at 30%, visual quality and uniqueness at 20% each, coherence and usability at 15% each. These scores guide selection; review assets in the interface they will serve.

Run locally

38

From a checkout with Nix and Devenv installed, enter the development shell, install the locked dependencies, then start the API and site together.

39 40

The Studio runs at localhost:5173/gui/. Its same-origin /api proxy reaches the Baste server on port 3456. Set BASTE_SITE_PORT and BASTE_API_PORT to change the ports. Storybook is an optional process on port 6006.

41

Use the native tasks for individual commands and checks. The full task list and environment setup live in the development guide.

42 43

46

Configure an account server

47

In Studio Settings, select Sign in / create profile. Not Organic creates or authenticates your account profile; a Baste design persona is a separate object. Manage your handle and account in the linked Not Organic portal.

48

The Baste server holds the provider session and DPoP key. The browser receives an HttpOnly Baste session cookie, a CSRF token and the profile's public DID and handle. The model picker loads the authorized catalog from your connected account.

49

Your wallet shows verified available credit and only the offers advertised by the provider. Select an offer to open checkout and review its current price before paying. On return, refresh the wallet: a redirect alone does not prove payment or credit delivery.

50

Hosted generation currently covers image suites and asset judging. Full UI kits still need your local SVG and video providers. An unverified, blocked or empty wallet prevents paid hosted generation; prompt drafts remain available.

51

Set a maximum spend for each hosted run, initially $1. The live budget plan counts image and judging requests, including QD candidates and final outputs. Reduce iterations, batch size or outputs per purpose until the plan fits your maximum and the server limit, or explicitly raise your maximum. These conservative ceilings are spending limits, not quoted prices.

52

For server operators: enable NOTORGANIC_ENABLED, set BASTE_PUBLIC_ORIGIN, and configure the issuer and authorization URL. Baste must be registered with Not Organic for its origin, callback, product audience, scopes and billing offers. Public checkout needs an HTTPS return origin.

53 54

The callback is /api/notorganic/callback on the Studio origin. Production hosting must proxy /api to the Baste server. Sessions live in server memory and expire after eight hours; restarting the server requires signing in again. Read the account integration guide for the deployment boundary.

Use your own provider keys

59

# Baste

**Interfaces cut to fit one person.**

![One interface, fitted to three personas](docs/fitting-loop.gif)

*Baste (v.) — to tack a garment together with long, loose stitches so it can be fitted before the final cut.*

Baste takes a persona's films, music, rooms, tools and obsessions, and from them drafts the design system, icons,
images and motion that fit. Palettes and typefaces are derived from the persona's cultural references, so no two
personas come out the same. Then it explores many candidates with quality-diversity search, judges them for
persona fit, and cuts the winners into production assets.

Now with **semantic version control for design systems** and **OpenPencil bridge** for editable design components.

## The Studio

```bash
npx baste gui        # local API on :3456 — then open the site's /gui route
```

The Studio (`site/`, route `/gui`) puts one persona at the centre: see it **wearing its own design** (a live
try-on of the same screen in its tokens, with contrast checks), export tokens, draft prompts and generate assets
with a staged progress view, pin a moodboard, read a decomposed brand kit, teach it your taste, and edit tokens
as an OpenPencil document. Without a local server it runs in demo mode on the built-in personas.

Start the API and Qwik Studio together from the repository root:

```bash
devenv tasks run baste:install
devenv up
```

Open `http://localhost:5173/gui/` for the Studio and `http://localhost:5173/docs/` for documentation.
The site proxies `/api` to the Baste API on port 3456. Storybook is opt-in.
See [local development](docs/development.md) for tasks, port overrides and verification boundaries.

## Not Organic accounts

Studio Settings includes profile creation/sign-in through Not Organic, the authorized model catalog,
wallet credit and advertised checkout offers. Hosted image generation and Jev judging use server-held
PKCE/DPoP authorization. Design personas are separate from the public account profile, and account-owned
design files are isolated by DID. Local CLI generation continues to use your selected provider keys.

Enable `NOTORGANIC_ENABLED=true` with an exact `BASTE_PUBLIC_ORIGIN` after registering Baste's product
and origin on the provider. Payments require provider-configured offers and an HTTPS return origin.
Source integration does not establish that a deployed sign-in or paid checkout works.
See [Not Organic integration](docs/notorganic.md) for the configuration and API contract.

# Local development

Use Nix and Devenv from the repository root. Native tasks run npm scripts with Node and install frozen dependencies using the root and site `package-lock.json` files.

```sh
devenv shell
devenv tasks run baste:install
devenv up
```

`devenv up` starts the Baste API on port 3456 and the Qwik site on port 5173. Open `http://localhost:5173/gui/` for the Studio or `http://localhost:5173/docs/` for documentation. The site proxies `/api` to the local API, keeping session cookies on one origin.

The bundled GUI served by `baste gui` is also available on the API port. It is a local legacy interface; the Qwik Studio owns the account, wallet and live hosted-model UI.

If the running site reports a missing import for a source file that now exists, restart just the site with `devenv processes restart site`. Vite can retain an SSR import failure when the importing file is updated before the new module is created. Check the rendered Studio and browser console after recovery: a development error page can return HTTP 200, so a successful health request alone does not verify the page.

## Saved projects

Open **Projects** in the Studio to give an application a brief and choose an audience persona. Projects retain their own audience snapshot, so editing a source persona does not silently alter an existing project. Each saved change creates a revision; restoring an earlier revision creates a new history entry.

Local projects are stored in `.baste/projects`. Hosted projects use the signed-in Not Organic account's directory under `.baste/accounts`. These private runtime files are ignored by Git. Concurrent changes return a conflict so the Studio can retain the draft and offer the latest saved version. Repeated requests with the same command ID do not create duplicate changes.

This is the first milestone of the [design partner plan](plans/design-partner.md). Generated characters, conversational refinement, GPT-Live and stop-motion performance are subsequent milestones.

An interrupted writer can leave a project lock behind. If a saved project keeps reporting that it is busy after a server crash, stop every Baste process using that storage before repairing the specific lock. From the same working directory as the server, after building:

```sh
devenv processes down
node dist/src/projects/repair-lock.js --project <project-id> --server-stopped
# For a hosted project, also supply its owner's DID:
node dist/src/projects/repair-lock.js --project <project-id> --account <owner-did> --server-stopped
devenv up
```

The repair preserves project history and command receipts. It refuses a live lock owner, a changed file or a symlink. The stopped-server precondition also covers other workers or replicas sharing this directory; run the appropriate local or hosted command once, then restart. This operation is deliberately unavailable to browser and agent callers.

## Tasks

| Task | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `baste:install` | Install root and site dependencies from their lockfiles |
| `baste:api` | Start the Baste API |
| `baste:site` | Start the Qwik site and Studio |
| `baste:docs` | Start the site for its `/docs/` route |
| `baste:storybook` | Start Storybook |
| `baste:dev` | Start the configured development processes with `devenv up` |
| `baste:build` | Build the CLI/package and site |
| `baste:typecheck` | Check root and site TypeScript |
| `baste:lint` | Check frontend lint rules |
| `baste:test` | Run existing root tests |
| `baste:check` | Run the configured validation tasks |
| `baste:storybook:build` | Build the component explorer |

```sh
devenv tasks list
devenv tasks run baste:typecheck
devenv tasks run baste:check
```

Storybook does not start by default. Enable its process when needed:

```sh
BASTE_WITH_STORYBOOK=1 devenv up
```

## Configuration

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and configure the providers you use. Do not commit `.env` or a config file containing private keys.

- `BASTE_API_PORT`: API process port, default `3456`.
- `BASTE_SITE_PORT`: Qwik development port, default `5173`.
- `BASTE_STORYBOOK_PORT`: Storybook port, default `6006`.
- `BASTE_WITH_STORYBOOK=1`: opt-in Storybook process.
- `BASTE_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`: exact browser origin for account callbacks and CSRF checks. Devenv sets `http://localhost:5173`; the standalone API defaults to `http://localhost:3456`. Set it explicitly when running the Qwik Studio outside Devenv, changing its port or serving a deployed Studio.

The Studio uses `/api` by default. Its Settings connection field supports an explicit API URL for local development. Account mode requires the configured Studio origin and a same-origin proxy. A public static site needs its hosting layer to route `/api` to Baste; a static build alone does not provide the account API.

For local generation, configure `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `QUIVER_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, and any other selected provider's settings. Run `baste config --init` for a local `baste.config.json`. Preview prompts with `baste generate cyberbotanist --dry-run` before spending provider credit.

The public persona conversation at `/#meet` uses authored replies when no conversation model is available. In local mode, `OPENAI_API_KEY` enables open-ended replies through `POST /api/converse/:id`; `BASTE_CONVERSATION_MODEL` selects the model (default `gpt-4o`). Restart the API after changing these values. `/api/health` reports `conversation.mode` as `ai` or `demo`. Account mode always disables this local-key path. Hosted AI conversation still needs a metered account transport; the public page labels its authored demo explicitly. Failed AI replies remain visible with a retry action, and never silently become demo replies.

Technical explanations, scoring, exports and local setup are at `/method/`. The public landing page introduces the personas. Lenis and Tempus run only on the landing and Method pages; inner chat and Studio scrollers remain native. The Method page's decorative Strands composition from shaders.com loads on visibility, with a static fallback for unavailable WebGPU and reduced motion. The heading reveal adapts React Bits' BlurText treatment to Qwik without adding a React runtime.

The public conversation reuses the Moss, Ren and Ada portraits from the October 8 companion workroom studies, recovered from worktree `73bc` through the local Entire session history. Their source prompts and asset provenance are in [companion-portraits.json](companion-portraits.json). They are illustrated example characters; the page does not claim that runtime portrait generation or the full Studio partner workflow is implemented. The conversation keeps the atelier typography and writing surface stable, while palette and type samples show each persona's design choices inline.

For the hosted account path, see [Not Organic integration](notorganic.md). Local CLI calls do not receive a browser's hosted account session.

## Verification boundaries

The fabric regression check exercises window resizing, a lost WebGL context, and touch viewport changes while scrolling. It checks that no resized canvas reaches paint before being redrawn, inspects the rendered background, and saves screenshots plus a report under `/tmp/baste-fabric-qa`:

```sh
rtk proxy node site/scripts/verify-fabric.mjs
```

Set `PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE` to an installed Playwright module if it is not on the project path. `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH`, `FABRIC_QA_URL` (default `http://localhost:5173`), and `FABRIC_QA_OUTPUT` are optional overrides. This is browser emulation; an actual mobile device remains a separate check.

Typechecks and builds verify code and compilation. They do not prove live sign-in, provider registration, funded inference, checkout, wallet delivery or webhook reconciliation. Record those separately after exercising a registered account and configured deployment. A prompt dry run proves prompt drafting only.

## Architecture

```
Baste
├── Persona Engine          # Cultural identity, influences, aesthetic
├── Design System           # CSS/Tailwind/Panda tokens from persona
├── QD Engine               # Quality Diversity search for diverse assets
├── LLM Judge               # Evaluates persona alignment
├── Version Control (NEW)   # Lix-inspired semantic versioning
│   ├── SQLite database     # Change-first, not snapshot-first
│   ├── Branches            # Parallel design exploration
│   ├── Cultural refs       # Images, screenshots, logos linked to history
│   └── .baste exporter     # Portable design system packages
└── OpenPencil Bridge (NEW) # Editable .pen documents round-trip
```

input.content:
---
name: hyperframes-render-env
description: How to run HyperFrames check/snapshot/render on this nix/guix Fedora host without Chrome or watchdog failures
metadata:
  type: reference
---

HyperFrames (pinned `hyperframes@0.8.145`, project `videos/baste-tour/`) needs three workarounds here:

- Prefix every command with `env -u LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. The shell's LD_LIBRARY_PATH holds nix alsa-lib plus a T3 AppImage mount, which breaks Chrome.
- The render preflight runs `ldd`, and guix's `ldd` reports missing libs. Keep a shim at `~/.cache/hf-shim/ldd -> /usr/bin/ldd` (not /tmp, which T3 restarts wipe) and put it first on PATH.
- A render is cancelled ("render_cancelled_parent_exited") when its launching shell exits, and T3 restarts kill background shells. Launch detached:
  `HYPERFRAMES_RENDER_DETACHED=1 setsid nohup bash -c 'env -u LD_LIBRARY_PATH PATH=$HOME/.cache/hf-shim:$PATH npx --yes hyperframes@0.8.145 render ... > renders/render.log 2>&1; echo "exit $?" >> renders/render.log' &`
  then wait with an until-loop on `^exit ` in the log.

With `--workers 8` the 74 s tour renders in about 90 s once Chrome starts.

Related: [[baste-dev-servers]]

result.output:
# Cartesia TTS (Bytes)

**Endpoint:** `POST https://api.cartesia.ai/tts/bytes`. It returns streamed audio bytes (`audio/*`, binary).

## Required headers
- **`Cartesia-Version`**: The only allowed value, and the default, is `2026-08-14`.
- **`Authorization: Bearer <token>`**: Use either an API key (`sk_car_...`, from play.cartesia.ai/keys) or a short-lived JWT access token for client-side use.
- **`Content-Type: application/json`**

## Request body

**Required fields:** `model_id`, `transcript`, `voice`, `output_format`

- **`model_id`**: One of `sonic-3.6` (default), `sonic-3.5`, `sonic-3` or `sonic-latest`.
- **`transcript`**: A string. The default is "Hi there, it's awesome to meet you."
- **`voice`**: Either a voice ID string or an object with a required `id`. The docs note that "Embeddings are not accepted in this API version."
- **`output_format`**: Choose one of these containers:
  - **`wav`**: `encoding` (default `pcm_s16le`) and `sample_rate` (default 44100).
  - **`mp3`**: `sample_rate` and `bit_rate` are both required. `bit_rate` is 32000, 64000, 96000, 128000 or 192000, with 128000 as the default.
  - **`raw`**: `encoding` and `sample_rate` are both required.
  - **Encodings:** `pcm_f32le`, `pcm_s16le`, `pcm_mulaw`, `pcm_alaw`.
  - **Sample rates:** 8000, 16000, 22050, 24000, 44100, 48000.
- **`language` / `locale`** (optional): Accepts codes like `en` or `en-GB`. Use only one of the two: "setting both returns a 400 error."
- **`accent`** (optional): Normally not needed. Use it only to give a multilingual voice an accent. The value must be one of the voice's listed `accents`.
- **`normalization`** (optional): `auto` (default), `off`, or a language/locale code.
- **`pronunciation_dict_id`** (optional): Works with `sonic-3` and newer models.
- **`generation_config`** (optional, `sonic-3` and newer):
  - **`volume`**: 0.5 to 2.0, default 1.
  - **`speed`**: 0.6 to 1.5, default 1.
  - **`emotion`**: Optional. The primary emotions are `neutral`, `calm`, `angry`, `content`, `sad` and `scared`, and many more are allowed (e.g., `happy`, `excited`, `curious`, `sarcastic`). If omitted, the model infers emotion from the transcript.

## Example
The page has no full example request. This one is assembled from the schema's defaults and example values:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.cartesia.ai/tts/bytes \
  -H "Cartesia-Version: 2026-08-14" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CARTESIA_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model_id": "sonic-3.6",
    "transcript": "Hi there, it'\''s awesome to meet you.",
    "voice": {"id": "db6b0ed5-d5d3-463d-ae85-518a07d3c2b4"},
    "language": "en",
    "output_format": {"container": "wav", "encoding": "pcm_s16le", "sample_rate": 44100},
    "generation_config": {"speed": 1.0, "volume": 1.0, "emotion": "calm"}
  }' --output out.wav
```

The extra context about Baste configuration isn't related to the Cartesia API, so I left it out.

input.prompt: Exact allowed values/ranges for generation_config.speed, volume, emotion; output_format options for mp3 (bit_rate etc.); any limits. Quote precisely.

result.output:
# Cartesia `/tts/bytes`: allowed values and limits

## `generation_config`
This only works on newer models: "Available on `sonic-3` and newer models; not available on earlier models."

- **`speed`** is a double with a default of 1. The spec says: "Valid values are between [0.6, 1.5] inclusive."
- **`volume`** is a double with a default of 1. The spec says: "Valid values are between [0.5, 2.0] inclusive."
- **`emotion`** is optional and has no default. If you leave it out, "the model interprets the emotional subtext of the transcript." The spec says: "The primary emotions are `neutral`, `calm`, `angry`, `content`, `sad`, `scared`." The full list of allowed values is: neutral, happy, excited, enthusiastic, elated, euphoric, triumphant, amazed, surprised, flirtatious, curious, content, peaceful, serene, calm, grateful, affectionate, trust, sympathetic, anticipation, mysterious, angry, mad, outraged, frustrated, agitated, threatened, disgusted, contempt, envious, sarcastic, ironic, sad, dejected, melancholic, disappointed, hurt, guilty, bored, tired, rejected, nostalgic, wistful, apologetic, hesitant, insecure, confused, resigned, anxious, panicked, alarmed, scared, proud, confident, distant, skeptical, contemplative, determined.

## `output_format`
You must set `container` to `wav`, `mp3` or `raw`.

- **mp3:** Both `sample_rate` and `bit_rate` are required.
  - `bit_rate` can be 32000, 64000, 96000, 128000 or 192000. The default is 128000.
  - `sample_rate` can be 8000, 16000, 22050, 24000, 44100 or 48000. The default is 44100.
  - The spec is inconsistent here: it gives defaults for both fields but also marks them as required.
- **wav:** `encoding` defaults to `pcm_s16le` and `sample_rate` defaults to 44100. The sample rates are the same as for mp3.
- **raw:** Both `encoding` and `sample_rate` are required.
- **Allowed encodings:** `pcm_f32le`, `pcm_s16le`, `pcm_mulaw`, `pcm_alaw`.

## Other limits and rules
- **Required fields:** `model_id`, `transcript`, `voice` and `output_format`.
- **`model_id`:** Must be `sonic-3.6` (the default), `sonic-3.5`, `sonic-3` or `sonic-latest`.
- **`language` and `locale`:** Use only one, because "setting both returns a 400 error."
- **`voice`:** "Embeddings are not accepted in this API version."
- **`pronunciation_dict_id`:** Only works with `sonic-3` and newer models.
- **`Cartesia-Version` header:** Required, and `2026-08-14` is the only allowed value.
- **Not covered by the page:** It gives no limit on transcript length and no rate limits.

content.text:
You were right: the tour on the site still had the old voice. It now has Elaine.

**What went wrong:** the render with Elaine's voice was fine, but I published to the site before that render had finished. The site was given the previous video, which still had Aria.

**The fix:** I published again from the finished render. `publish.mjs` now refuses to run until the render log ends in `exit 0`, so this can't happen again.

**How I checked:** hashing the video files doesn't settle which voice they contain, because every re-encode produces a different hash even with identical audio. Instead I compared the narration at 0:19 in each version against the old and new voice recordings. The comparison script is `/tmp/voice-compare/which.py`; 1.0 is a match.

| File | Matches Elaine | Matches Aria |
|---|---|---|
| Earlier renders (before the icon fix and after it) | 0.03 | 0.98 |
| Latest render | 0.98 | 0.03 |
| Site copy, before re-publishing | 0.03 | 0.98 |
| **Site copy, now** | **0.98** | **0.03** |

`/tmp/voice-compare/tour-new.mp3` has been regenerated from the published tour (different hash from `tour-old.mp3`), so the two clips should now sound clearly different.

Yes, Cartesia has male voices. I made samples of two, **Theo** and **Clyde**, reading the same two tour lines as the current voices, so you can compare them directly. The files are named by voice and all have different hashes:

| File | Voice | Length |
|---|---|---|
| `/tmp/voices/aria-elevenlabs-old.mp3` | Aria (ElevenLabs), the original | 14.7 s |
| `/tmp/voices/elaine-cartesia-current.mp3` | Elaine (Cartesia), now on the site | 16.7 s |
| `/tmp/voices/theo-cartesia-male.mp3` | Theo: "steady, enunciating, confident young male for narrations" | 15.4 s |
| `/tmp/voices/clyde-cartesia-male.mp3` | Clyde: "gentle, measured male voice with warmth and clarity for storytelling" | 16.0 s |

Each file reads "Most interfaces are cut for… A person does." and then "Then it fits an interface to them…". The ffmpeg warnings in the output are only noise from joining the clips; all four files play normally.

Theo is the quickest speaker of these, so he'd fit the tour's cuts most easily. Clyde runs about Elaine's pace, which also fits.

Tell me which one you'd like, or ask for more male options (for example a deeper documentary voice such as Damon or Carl). I'll then re-voice the tour and both English walkthroughs and confirm the voice in each published file before telling you it's done.

Understood, I'll leave the voices mixed for now.

The tour on the site now has Theo. I checked the published file against both voices: it matches Theo (0.98), not Elaine (0.05).

| Video | Voice |
|---|---|
| Tour (1:14, home page and Studio guide) | **Theo** (Cartesia) |
| Short Studio walkthrough (0:29) | **Theo** (Cartesia) |
| Long English walkthrough (1:53) | **Elaine** (Cartesia) |
| French walkthrough | Unchanged (original voice) |

The long walkthrough stayed on Elaine because the Cartesia account ran out of credit partway through switching it. Cartesia returned "quota_exceeded" after 19 of its 22 sentences, so the published file is still the complete Elaine version.

To move it to Theo later, top up Cartesia and run `node scripts/revoice-walkthrough.mjs --skate`. It reuses the 19 sentences already made, so only three new requests are needed.

On ElevenLabs v4 from your earlier message: I didn't use it for any of these. If Cartesia's credit is a problem, I can add ElevenLabs as a second option in `scripts/cartesia.mjs`; it would bill your fal account.

The developer docs, `docs/development.md` and the tour's brief and script files now name Theo as the narrator.
